newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek PM inaugurates natural gas project.
newsitem.headline: Greek PM inaugurates natural gas project.

text.p: Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis inaugurated a natural gas pipeline which will bring Russian gas to Greece.
Russian Energy minister Peter Rodionov and the president of state gas company Gazprom attended the inauguration ceremony at Elefsis, an industrial city 20 kilometers (12.5 miles) west of Athens.
"This is the biggest energy project since Greece got electricity and it will be most advantageous to our country," Simitis said in his inauguration speech.
He said that by creating a distribution network of a cheap and environment-friendly fuel, industrial zones will benefit and production costs will be lowered.

"Natural gas is a cheap source of energy. It will diminish our dependence on petrol and will create security for the future. It will also create new jobs and will boost exports of Greek goods and services," he added.
The project is budgeted at 700 billion drachmas ($2.8 billion). The main pipeline was built in 1995 and first gas flow was in September.
On November 15, Hellenic Sugar Industry's Larisa plant was connected to the pipeline, the first industrial unit in Greece to use natural gas as fuel, the Public Gas Corporation of Greece (DEPA) said.
Simitis said the gas project was only part of a continuing cooperation between Greece and Russia. The two countries signed a new energy pact on Monday.
